label: D2 after choosing a2 and reaching S2 (common a2->S2), sparse subset
explanation: Active only at D2 (85% of mass) and GO (15%), never at D1. Essentially every D2 activation is on a trial where the agent chose a2 and reached S2 via the common transition (in_action=2, in_state=2); it is silent after a1 or on reaching S1. GO activations occur only when the upcoming choice is a2 (the agent own choice, legitimate). The predicate D2 & a2 & S2 (all observed at D2) captures ~85% of mass but precision is very low (~6%): the unit fires on only a small fraction of such steps. Firing is further concentrated where the model value output is high (>8.1; adding this gives P 0.16, R 0.74), policy logit strongly favours a2 (-8.9..-4.4; P 0.23, F1 0.35), and in episode trials 10-60 (almost none after trial 70); it is more likely when the previous trial was rare (prev_common 0). Identical trial contexts at different window positions often get different activations, so the selection among a2->S2 steps is not well captured by task variables. Recorded the simple observed-only predicate; a GO a2 clause raises recall to ~1.0 but halves precision. Magnitudes are tiny (thresholded update gate); largest values seen at D2 a2->S2c following rare or unrewarded trials.
